clue.text: Do we hear an order for long drinks on the rocks ?

indicators.note: the question asks whether we hear something, so the word ordered is to be taken by its sound

parts.note: ordering 'quarts!' asks for drinks by the large measure of two pints

explanation.surface: A barman wonders whether he heard a request for big drinks served over ice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the rocks' pretends to mean served with ice; here it says the answer is found in rocks, being a common rock-forming mineral.
explanation.definitionFit: This hard crystalline mineral is one of the commonest constituents of granite and other rocks.

clue.text: Edict that applies to us as to Asia

parts.note: to a British setter 'us' is the United Kingdom, UK
taken as written
Asia lies in the East, abbreviated E

explanation.surface: A decree is said to bind Britain just as it binds Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: A ukase was a decree of the Russian tsar, an empire spanning Europe and Asia, which helps the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A ukase is a tsarist decree, and by extension any arbitrary order from on high.

clue.text: S.E. European country made sane by one country in collapse

indicators.note: something made sane loses its madness, so the word for madness is struck out of the country

parts.note: Rumania is the older spelling of Romania, in south-east Europe
one is the Roman numeral I
a country is a nation

explanation.surface: A Balkan state is cured of madness by a single nation amid a breakdown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made sane' removes MANIA (madness) from RUMANIA, leaving RU.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruination is utter ruin or downfall, the state of having fallen apart.

clue.text: Puck's express work of subdivision ?

definitions.meaning: in A Midsummer Night's Dream Puck promises to put a girdle round the earth in forty minutes: speedy encircling
dividing land into areas set aside for different uses

explanation.surface: The fairy's rapid task turns out to be carving something into parts.
explanation.walkthrough: A zone is literally a girdle, so girdling the earth as Puck boasts is zoning it.
explanation.definitionFit: Encircling the globe as with a belt, and planners' division of land into districts, are both senses of the word.

clue.text: Moroccan maids of the mountains act as men in Westerns

parts.note: maids are female, so each is a 'she'
the Riffs are the Berber people of the Rif mountains of northern Morocco

explanation.surface: Mountain girls from Morocco play the parts of cowboy-film heroes.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Moroccan maids of the mountains' as female Riffs, SHE plus RIFFS; 'Moroccan' places the mountains, the Rif range.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawmen wearing a star, the county peace officers, are stock figures of cowboy films.

clue.text: A fair show, but weren't the gods angry !

definitions.meaning: a fairground booth where visitors fire at targets
theatre's cheap top seats are the gods or gallery, and an angry gallery would be firing at the actors

explanation.surface: A fun-fair entertainment provokes the wrath of heaven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The gods' are the highest theatre seats, also called the gallery; 'but' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A booth at a fair where people fire at targets, and a theatre's top tier taking aim in fury, are both pictured.

clue.text: Large deerstalker.

parts.note: not the cap but a big hunting dog used in Norway to track moose

explanation.definitionFit: This big Scandinavian hunting breed was bred to track and hold moose for the hunter.

clue.text: I buy and sell to perfection

parts.note: to buy and sell goods is to deal in them

explanation.surface: A trader claims his buying and selling is flawless.
explanation.definitionFit: An ideal is a standard of flawlessness, perfection as conceived in the mind.

clue.text: Stone Age gun .?

parts.note: a musket fired by a struck stone, as if a firearm from prehistory

explanation.definitionFit: An old musket whose charge was lit by a spark from a stone striking steel.

clue.text: Allowances were made for the contents of this publication

definitions.text: Allowances were made for the contents of this publication

parts.words: Allowances were made for the contents of this publication
parts.note: the 'allowances' are the wartime rations, and the booklet held coupons for them

explanation.definitionFit: A wartime booklet of coupons entitling the holder to fixed rations of food and goods.

clue.text: Get out of this !

parts.note: reads as an exclamation of disbelief, but describes the marked way out of a building

explanation.definitionFit: A door or way out, the thing one goes through to leave.

clue.text: Hickory head

parts.note: nut is slang for head, so a hickory's head is a nut from that tree family

explanation.definitionFit: The pecan tree is a species of hickory, and its edible kernel in a shell is its fruit.

clue.text: A devotee of an Orange body?

definitions.meaning: a lay person dedicated to religious life in a monastery
describing a sphere flattened at the poles, like the shape of an orange

explanation.surface: A loyal supporter belongs to an Ulster Orange lodge.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital O suggests the Protestant Orange Order; it is the fruit, whose squashed round shape is the geometric sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a person offered to monastic life and the flattened-sphere shape of the earth or a fruit carry the word.

clue.text: One politician returns to the island

indicators.note: returns sends the whole run back the way it came, so it is read right to left

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
Lab is short for a Labour politician

explanation.surface: A lone MP goes back to his holiday island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returns' turns ILAB round, giving the Indonesian island.
explanation.definitionFit: Bali is an island of Indonesia, east of Java.

clue.text: Signature' of an American car chart ?

parts.note: auto is the American word for a car
a graph is a chart

explanation.surface: A driver wonders whether a signature belongs on a chart of US cars.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's handwritten name, especially one given to a fan, is this.

clue.text: Sister's déjeuner ?

parts.note: a nun's version of luncheon, the French déjeuner, with the opening letter made into that of 'nun'

explanation.walkthrough: The old word for a light midday snack looks like luncheon taken by a nun (sister).
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for a light snack taken between meals, around noon.

clue.text: Problems of pain

definitions.meaning: troublesome difficulties or worries
throbbing pains in the skull

explanation.surface: Someone lists the difficulties that suffering brings.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a nuisance or worry and an ache in the cranium go by the word.

clue.text: High regard of a flower

definitions.meaning: a view from above, as a bird would see it
a name for the speedwell and other small bright-centred flowers

explanation.surface: A flower is held in great esteem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High regard' sounds like esteem; it is a look from on high, as in a bird's-eye view.
explanation.definitionFit: A view from high overhead and several small wild plants such as the primrose relative both bear the name.

clue.text: Fine but hardly conducive to sensibility

definitions.meaning: strikingly beautiful or excellent
knocking someone senseless, the opposite of keeping their senses

explanation.surface: Something excellent is not, alas, good for refined feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sensibility' suggests delicate feeling; read it as being conscious, which a blow that dazes removes.
explanation.definitionFit: Both gorgeous and knocking a person out cold are senses of the word.

clue.text: Seeks for a sign of potassium in a moke

indicators.note: the symbol is placed in the middle of the donkey word, inside it

parts.note: moke is slang for a donkey, an ass
K is the chemical symbol for potassium

explanation.surface: A chemist hunts for potassium inside a donkey.
explanation.walkthrough: Moke is British slang for a donkey.
explanation.definitionFit: To request or inquire after something is to seek it.

clue.text: Didn't go but kept one going

definitions.meaning: remained in place rather than leaving
supported or propped up, as a mast is held by stays

explanation.surface: Someone stayed put yet kept another person on the move.
explanation.walkthrough: A stay is a rope or brace that supports, so 'stayed' can mean propped up; 'but' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Remained behind, and also braced or held up as by a support, both use the word.

clue.text: An insatiable appetite of the ayes

parts.note: an is the article A
greed is an appetite that cannot be satisfied

explanation.surface: Those voting yes display boundless hunger.
explanation.walkthrough: When the ayes have it in a vote, the motion is consented to.
explanation.definitionFit: A motion carried by those saying yes is consented to by the house.

clue.text: She looks to' be in the fifties even seen briefly outside

indicators.note: the shortened word sits on either side of the numerals, outside them
the word is shown in its clipped poetic form, with a letter dropped

parts.note: even is shortened in poetry to e'en
L is the Roman numeral for fifty, so two of them make fifties

explanation.surface: A woman appears to be in her fifties, even at a glance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seen briefly' turns EVEN into poetic E'EN, which goes 'outside' LL.
explanation.definitionFit: Ellen is a woman's name, so it can stand for a female person.

clue.text: Lack of energy to tidy the garth in the meadow

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are put in the meadow word, inside it

parts.note: a ley is grassland, a meadow

indicators.note: tidying rearranges things into a new order

explanation.surface: A gardener lacks the drive to tidy the yard in the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To tidy' rearranges GARTH into THARG, which goes 'in' LEY. A garth is an enclosed yard or garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Lethargy is sluggishness, a want of vigour or drive.

clue.text: Naturally a low place for a blow-out.

definitions.meaning: a deep natural ravine between hills
blow-out is slang for a huge meal, a feast

explanation.surface: A ravine is the obvious spot for a slap-up meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow-out' suggests a tyre burst; it is a feast, and to gorge is to stuff oneself; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A steep narrow valley and a greedy feed both carry the word.

clue.text: Defence post

definitions.meaning: armour made of linked metal rings
letters delivered by the postal service

explanation.surface: A defensive position is manned.
explanation.definitionFit: Chain armour and letters delivered to the door share the name.

clue.text: Like Mad Hervey: we're ubiquitous

indicators.note: mad letters are wild and disordered, so they are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: People like Mad Hervey boast that they turn up all over the place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mad' rearranges HERVEY plus WERE. The definition is loose in part of speech, the adverb standing for 'found all over'.
explanation.definitionFit: Found in every place, which is what ubiquitous means.

clue.text: Law ! Pug's head's trapped !

definitions.meaning: a division of the High Court dealing in equity
a pug is a boxer, and a fighter whose head is held under his opponent's arm is said to be in this

explanation.surface: Someone cries out as their dog gets its head stuck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pug' looks like the dog; it is short for pugilist, a boxer.
explanation.definitionFit: A court of equity, and old boxing slang for a head held helpless in an armlock, both use the word.

clue.text: Was quick to draw the line

definitions.meaning: rushed or hurried
marked with dashes, strokes of the pen

explanation.surface: Someone hurried to set a limit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw the line' sounds like setting a limit; here it is literally making strokes; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Rushed off, and wrote a stroke of punctuation, both share the word.
